subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Hydrogen bonds form between water molecules because water is:
options: A polar molecule with partially charged regions
A molecule held together by ionic bonds
questions.explain: Oxygen is more electronegative than hydrogen, giving water partial charges (dipolarity) that allow hydrogen bonding between molecules.

questions.q: The attraction between water molecules themselves is called:
questions.explain: Cohesion is water-to-water attraction via hydrogen bonds; adhesion is attraction to other surfaces.

questions.q: The continuous column of water pulled up the xylem of a tall tree depends primarily on:
questions.explain: Cohesion holds the water column together under tension while adhesion helps water cling to vessel walls (cohesion–tension theory).

questions.q: Water has a high specific heat capacity, which means it:
questions.explain: Extensive hydrogen bonding means large energy input is needed to raise water's temperature, stabilising aquatic habitats and body temperature.

questions.q: Sweating cools the body effectively because water has a high:
questions.explain: Evaporating water absorbs a large amount of heat energy from the skin, producing a strong cooling effect.

questions.q: Water is an excellent solvent for glucose and ions because:
options: Its polarity lets it surround charged and polar particles
It forms covalent bonds with solutes
questions.explain: Polar water molecules cluster around ions and polar solutes (hydration shells), dissolving them.

questions.q: Pond skaters can walk on water because hydrogen bonding produces:
questions.explain: Cohesion at the surface creates a 'skin' (surface tension) strong enough to support small organisms.

questions.q: Why is glucose transported dissolved in blood plasma while lipids are carried in lipoproteins?
options: Glucose is hydrophilic but lipids are hydrophobic
questions.explain: Polar/soluble glucose dissolves in plasma, whereas nonpolar lipids are insoluble in water and need carrier proteins.

questions.q: Compared with Earth, the properties of water are often used to assess the possibility of extraterrestrial life because water:
options: Is a stable liquid solvent over a wide temperature range
questions.explain: Liquid water's solvent and thermal properties make it central to the search for life beyond Earth.

questions.q: Adhesion of water is best described as attraction between water and:
questions.explain: Adhesion is attraction to different, usually polar, surfaces (e.g. xylem walls), aiding capillary action.

questions.q: A single DNA nucleotide is made of:
options: Deoxyribose, a phosphate group and a nitrogenous base
Ribose, a phosphate and an amino acid
Glycerol, a phosphate and a base
questions.explain: Each DNA nucleotide has a deoxyribose sugar, one phosphate and one of four nitrogenous bases.

questions.q: In DNA, adenine always pairs with:
questions.explain: A–T pair via two hydrogen bonds; G–C pair via three (complementary base pairing).

questions.q: The two strands of a DNA molecule are 'antiparallel', meaning they:
questions.explain: One strand runs 5'→3' and its partner runs 3'→5', a feature essential for replication and transcription.

questions.q: The pentose sugar found in RNA is:
questions.explain: RNA contains ribose (with an –OH on carbon 2), whereas DNA contains deoxyribose.

questions.q: Which base is found in RNA but not in DNA?
questions.explain: RNA uses uracil in place of thymine; uracil pairs with adenine.

questions.q: If one DNA strand reads 5'-A T G C-3', the complementary strand reads:
questions.explain: Complementary, antiparallel pairing gives T-A, A-T, C-G, G-C read in the 3'→5' direction.

questions.q: Adjacent nucleotides in a DNA strand are joined by covalent bonds between:
options: The phosphate of one and the sugar (3' carbon) of the next
questions.explain: Phosphodiester bonds link the 5' phosphate of one nucleotide to the 3' carbon of the sugar of the next, forming the sugar–phosphate backbone.

questions.q: Complementary base pairing gives the DNA double helix a constant width because:
options: A purine always pairs with a pyrimidine
questions.explain: Pairing a double-ring purine with a single-ring pyrimidine keeps the diameter uniform along the helix.

questions.q: The main biological role of DNA is to:
questions.explain: DNA's stable double-stranded structure allows reliable storage and inheritance of genetic information.

questions.q: Chargaff found that in DNA the amount of adenine equals the amount of thymine. This is a direct consequence of:
questions.explain: Because A pairs only with T (and G with C), %A = %T and %G = %C in double-stranded DNA.
